## CEO overview

What is changing: Firstmate gains an explicit safety option for callers that send text to a worker.
  With `--inbox-only`, text is stored as a durable message even when it starts with `/` or `$`, while callers that omit the option keep the existing routing behavior.
Why it matters: Browser and third-party callers can pass untrusted text without accidentally placing it in a command-aware composer and without trying to classify the text themselves.
Customer or business impact: This creates the safety boundary needed to restore the Firstmate Control message composer in a separate change, while this pull request deliberately leaves that interface disabled.
Risk and rollout: Risk is low because the option is additive, applies only to task selectors, and rejects explicit worker targets, key input, and empty messages instead of silently changing their behavior.
  Synchronize this narrative into the live pull request description while preserving its machine-owned `## Pipeline` section, then require every hosted check on the resulting final head.

## What changed technically

- Added `--inbox-only` parsing to `bin/fm-send.sh` for text addressed through a task selector resolved from the active Firstmate home.
- Routed opted-in text through the existing durable inbox serializer and constant doorbell path regardless of whether its first character normally selects the typed plane.
- Preserved the existing typed routing for slash commands and Codex dollar invocations when the option is absent.
- Added executable coverage proving slash-prefixed and dollar-prefixed bodies are stored unchanged and never typed when the option is present.

## Module-boundary decision

Module-boundary decision: Current modules retained because message-plane selection belongs in `bin/fm-send.sh`, where target identity, worker type, typed delivery, and durable inbox delivery are already resolved.
  No new routing component or Control-interface change is needed in this pull request.
